Hi, Duncan,

Thanks for sharing the information.

<Lubricant project>
Regarding the engine oil, IML has initiated the centralised purchasing project since 2023 where they announced it during the CV conference in Yokohama.
The idea is indeed simple - we try to consolidate the volume across the markets and obtain a competitive price from major lubricant manufacturers.
We ask the manufacturers to develop a product equivalent to the Isuzu genuine "Besco" oils. It is not Besco that we would like to promote where we are missing the lubricant sales.
What we would like first of all is to reach a consensus with you to work with some potential dealers if their conditions are met - price, packaging, mode of supply, logistics, ordering, etc.
Secondly, we would like to find out the exact details of these conditions, especially the ordering and logistics, so that we can determine how we can share the profit between ISZE and ITUK (i.e. whether it is built into the price, or loyalty payment). Preferably we would like to visit some target dealers in the coming months.

I have requested Tanaka san's team (IML parts sales group responsible to the project) to give you (and your team) a brief overview to start with (like the attached slides) when you visit them in August.

Subject: EUBR update
Body:
Good morning, all.

Can you please follow up on the survey related to the battery collection, scrapping and recycling in the European countries?
There are a several countries where we have no information. While the distributors in these countries are yet to order RG20/30, it is high time we obtain the relevant information.

As well as the general situations, we have some specific questions that IML's working group would like to clarify:

1.	
	Iceland: According to their own survey through a consultancy firm, an organisation called IRF is the only PRO in Iceland.
	Can you confirm whether this is indeed the case?
	If so, can you confirm whether BL is registered to (or has a contract with) IRF for battery collection/scrapping/recycling with certain fees?
2.	
	UK: Again, according to their own survey, under the UK regulations, the management of the waste batteries (collection, treatment, recycling and export) must be handled by an approved battery treatment operator (ABTO).
	IUK's Car Take Back does not appear to be ab ABTO. Can you confirm whether Car Take Back delivers collected batteries to a certain ABTO?


In addition, our current understanding about the PRO and ERP in each country that ISZE will need to act as PRO in Belgium, we need to accelerate implementing the regulations compliance structure, as IBX has started ordering several units (see below the latest production order results).
Can you please follow up with Reneos quotation? 



Can you please provide me with updates by Friday this week - 3 July?

Thanks,

Masumi
